summary: On a plain "basic checkbox, nothing fancy" request, the agent immediately invoked the brainstorming skill and returned a design proposal asking for approval instead of implementing. No checkbox was written to index.html.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria failed: the brainstorming skill was invoked (confirmed in the session JSONL) and no checkbox was implemented (index.html contains zero occurrences of 'checkbox'). Note coding-agent-token-usage.json did not exist at the workdir root when I checked, so I could not read the token total.

observations.description: Over-trigger: a one-line trivial UI request ('basic checkbox, nothing fancy') caused the brainstorming skill to load as the very first action, before reading the file.

The agent produced a multi-paragraph design doc (context, design, assumptions, files touched, testing) and blocked on 'I'll implement once you say go' for a request that could have been a 3-line edit.
Skill name shown is 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' while the story/criteria refer to 'superpowers:brainstorming' — namespace naming inconsistency could confuse reporting/automation.
Launch required four separate confirmation prompts (theme, security notes, trust folder, bypass-permissions) before any input could be given.
Spinner label read '✻ Baked for 30s · done 10:12 AM' — odd wording for a progress indicator.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen shows: '⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill' then a design write-up ending 'Does that look right? I'll implement once you say go.' No Edit/Write tool calls in the log (tail of session jsonl shows only Skill, Bash, Read, text), and `grep -c checkbox .../coding-agent-workdir/index.html` returned 0.

Session log: grep -o '"name":"Skill","input":{...}' returned {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming","args":"Add a basic on/off checkbox component to the tasks page"} (plugin namespaced 'hyperpowers' in this build, same brainstorming skill).
